page: Amazon Web Services r7gd.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance built on the ARMv8 64-bit architecture. Powered by custom AWS Graviton3 Neoverse-V1 processors, it delivers 64 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.6 GHz with one thread per core. The server provides 512 GB of DDR5 system memory, establishing a generous 8 GB per core ratio. Hardware resources also include 3,800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance store volumes and 30 Gbps baseline networking throughput, eliminating hypervisor overhead for latency-critical deployments.

Benchmark results show strong execution in heavily parallelized and memory-bound tasks. The system achieves top-tier scores in multi-core metrics, registering 21,157 in Geekbench multi-core testing and 59,649 in Clang compilation. DDR5 memory subsystem performance is equally high, reflected in a PassMark memory score of 3,197.46 and cached read bandwidth reaching 6,198.58 GB/s. For caching workloads, it sustains over 102 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, single-thread performance benchmarks, such as Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core tests, fall into median ranges, indicating that execution efficiency relies on parallel concurrency.

From an efficiency perspective, the custom arm64 architecture combined with direct bare-metal hardware access delivers substantial compute density and memory capacity per allocated resource. However, workloads relying on x86-specific SIMD extensions, such as AVX-512, are not supported on this platform. With its large memory footprint, high memory bandwidth, and attached NVMe storage, r7gd.metal fits in-memory caching systems like Redis or Memcached, transactional database clusters, massive CI/CD compilation pipelines, and high-volume static web serving environments.
description: Amazon Web Services r7gd.metal is a bare-metal memory-optimized server powered by 64 dedicated AWS Graviton3 cores based on the ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 architecture running at 2.6 GHz. Operating without hypervisor overhead, it pairs 64 physical cores with 512 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It also integrates 3,800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and 30 Gbps of baseline networking capacity. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates exceptional multi-threaded performance, recording top-tier results in software compilation and PassMark memory operations, alongside strong throughput exceeding 102 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Single-thread processing remains average, indicating that performance scales best across distributed, highly parallel tasks. With direct bare-metal access, high memory bandwidth, and low-latency attached NVMe storage, r7gd.metal is targeted at large-scale in-memory key-value stores, relational and NoSQL databases, continuous integration build clusters, and data-intensive batch processing.
